start.text: Drums call the village to the fair. Dilip hurries to the stage and steps on the little bamboo voice-reed, the boli, with a crack. Kamla's show starts in one hour.
start.speaker: dilip

choices.text: Slip the broken boli into a sleeve and say nothing
Run to the market to find a new one before anyone notices
Show Kamla the broken boli and say it was your clumsy foot

hidden.text: Kamla reaches for the boli, finds splinters, and her brows climb. "Now we lose time, and I lose my trust in you." She sends Dilip off to the market anyway.
hidden.speaker: kamla

told.text: Kamla turns the pieces over. "Honest feet, at least. A boli is two slivers of bamboo and a stretched band, but only dry, hollow cane will sing." She points to the market lane.
told.speaker: kamla

market.text: The lane is thick with sellers. A potter shouts about jars, a sweet-maker about laddus, and an old weaver sits among cane baskets. Which stall can help a puppeteer?
market.speaker: dilip

choices.text: The potter: clay jars ring and chime
The sweet-maker: he surely knows every trick of sugar and reeds
The basket weaver: she works with cane every day

detour.text: The seller laughs kindly. "Clay and sugar never sang a note. Try the basket weaver." The drums have begun and Dilip's sandals slap faster over the stones.

weaver.text: The weaver holds up three lengths of cane. "Choose the one that will sing. Tap it and listen: green and bent, dry and hollow, or thick and solid?"
weaver.speaker: weaver

show.text: The curtain parts and Kamla's strings are in a knot, one dancer's skirt tangled with the king's crown. The crowd murmurs. Kamla looks at Dilip: "You have clever hands. Quick."
show.speaker: kamla

choices.text: Pull hard at the top of the knot and hope it frees
Let Kamla fix it while the drummers fill the gap
Lay the bar down and free each string from the top, one at a time

applause.text: The show runs and the puppets bow to loud clapping. A child calls out, "Who gave the dancer her voice?" The crowd turns to Dilip, then to the basket stall far back.
applause.speaker: kamla

choices.text: Take every cheer yourself and bow low
Call the weaver forward to share the bow

finale.text: Lamps swing, sweets are passed along the rows and the dancer puppet twirls once more. Kamla tucks the new boli into her belt and laughs, ready for the next fair.

endings.headline: The voice of the fair
endings.text: A kept promise, a clever ear and a shared bow: the dancer sings.

endings.headline: The show goes on
endings.text: The strings are freed and the voice is found, though the evening was a scramble.

endings.headline: A thin little show
endings.text: The puppets dance, but the voice squeaks and the crowd drifts away early.
